summary: Intermittent cross-region hop observed while 'residency: strict' enabled during neighbor-region maintenance; customer requests routing behaviour and mitigations
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports periodic spikes in p95/p99 latency and a small number of session-level timeouts during a scheduled maintenance window in the neighboring EU region. They have 'residency: strict' enabled and expect no cross-border hops for inference. The customer observed that some requests were routed to eu-north for short intervals, causing token latencies to jump and triggering their internal alarms.

Impact:
- Intermittent latency spikes p95 -> p99 on a subset (~0.6%) of requests during windows of 2-8 minutes.
- 504 and 5xx errors for sessions that hit the rerouted path under heavy load.
- Customer concern: potential data egress from eu-west and compliance implications despite strict residency setting.

Requested outcome:
- Clear explanation of why routing chose eu-north while residency: strict was set.
- Confirmation whether any customer data left eu-west at rest or in transit outside the region.
- Suggested mitigation/workarounds and config changes to prevent this class of reroute during neighbor maintenance.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer traffic pattern: steady throughput 40rps with bursts to 120rps for short periods
Enable residency: strict and pin model version to redwood-open-3b in eu-west
Trigger a maintenance window on nearby region (simulated by removing capacity from eu-west-edge nodes or scheduling maintenance)
Observe routing decision logs, p95/p99 metrics, and any 5xx/504 counts during the window
observed_logs: Customer provided sample: 18/120 requests in sample window saw downstream hop to eu-north (X-Route-Path header)
comments: 2026-03-10 | Maya Singh (customer): We expected strict residency to prevent any cross-region routing. We saw headers indicating eu-north and our compliance team is worried about egress. Please advise ASAP.
2026-03-10 | Support (Lina Moreno): Acknowledged; gathering routing logs and escalation to SRE. Can you confirm the project/model pins and any recent rollout config changes?

2026-03-11 | Tomas Alvarez (assigned): Initial SRE triage suggests a failover path triggered by maintenance drain on a subset of edge pools. Collecting decision traces to confirm whether data left the EU region.

2026-03-12 | SRE (Anita Patel): Traces show control-plane decision to re-route to eu-north for active KV-cache shards when local capacity fell below threshold. No persisted model artifacts were copied; encrypted request bodies traversed an encrypted link between eu-west and eu-north (TLS).
investigation_notes: Control-plane policy: 'residency: strict' is implemented as a strong preference but allows temporary intra-EEA routing to adjacent regions under emergency capacity pressure to preserve availability. This was not well-documented in customer-facing docs.

We found two contributing factors: (1) an autoscaler bug in eu-west-edge that under-allocated during drain, increasing capacity_pressure triggers; (2) the routing policy had a 'grace failover' path to nearest EEA region to avoid 100% request failure.

Data residency assessment: TLS was used for inter-region hops and no storage of customer plaintext data outside eu-west occurred. Model KV shards are cached, but no durable replica was written in eu-north during these events.
Observed latency delta: median token latency increased ~450ms for rerouted requests; p99 increased up to ~2.8s for affected samples.
Relevant logs and traces: link to internal trace set (confluence/grafana references below).
resolution:
Temporary: increased strictness of routing preference for this customer to disallow cross-region failover unless the customer explicitly opts-in; SRE applied a customer-level routing override to block eu-north paths during the next 7-day window.

Permanent: engineering will update routing policy docs to clarify behavior of 'residency: strict' and add a new configuration flag 'residency: strict-absolute' that avoids cross-region hops at the cost of returning 5xx when local capacity is insufficient. A PR to add the flag and docs has been opened and linked.

Customer asked for a written attestation that no persistent customer data left the region — security provided a short statement and artifacts.
